title: The First Revelation
teaser: He was forty years old. Alone in a cave. Then an angel said: Read. And everything changed.

layers.title: The Cave
layers.subtitle: Three years of solitude before prophethood
layers.content:
When Prophet Muhammad was nearly forty, he was accustomed to passing long hours in seclusion, meditating and reflecting over all aspects of creation around him. He used to provide himself with Saweeq (barley porridge) and water and then head for the hills near Makkah.

His favourite retreat was a cave named Hira' in the Mount An-Noor — only two miles from Makkah, a small cave four arm-lengths long and 1.75 arm-lengths wide. He would devote most of his time, and Ramadan in particular, to worship and meditate on the universe around him.

His heart was restless about the moral evils and idolatry widespread among his people. Seclusion and reflective meditation was a preliminary stage to the period of grave responsibilities that he was to shoulder very soon. It was an intense period of privacy which lasted for three years prior to the beginning of his mission.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 96:1 — Read in the name of your Lord who created
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: Iqra
layers.subtitle: The word that changed history
layers.content:
Aisha narrated: The first initiation of revelation for Allah's Messenger assumed the form of true dreams. At length, unexpectedly, the Truth came to him while in the cave. The angel came to him and said: Recite. I cannot recite, he said.

The Prophet described: Then he took me and embraced me tightly and then let me go and repeated the order: Recite. I cannot recite, said I; and once again he squeezed me and let go me until I was exhausted. Then he said: Recite. I said: I cannot recite. He squeezed me for a third time and then let me go and said: Read! In the Name of your Lord, Who has created all that exists, has created man from a clot. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous. (Quran 96:1-3)

The Prophet repeated these Verses, trembling with fear. He came back to his wife Khadijah and said: Cover me, cover me. They covered him until he regained composure. He informed Khadijah of the incident and said he was frightened.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 96:1-3 — Read! In the Name of your Lord who created
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: Khadijah's Response
layers.subtitle: The first believer and her words
layers.content:
Khadijah tried to soothe him and reassured him saying: Allah will never disgrace you. You unite relations of the womb, bear the burden of the weak, help the poor and the needy, you entertain the guests and endure hardships in the path of truthfulness.

She set out with the Prophet to her cousin Waraqah bin Nawfal, who had embraced Christianity in the pre-Islamic period. He was an old blind man. Khadijah said: My cousin! Listen to your nephew! Waraqah said: O my nephew! What did you see?

Allah's Messenger told him what happened. Waraqah replied: This is the Namus — the angel entrusted with Divine Secrets — that Allah sent to Moses. I wish I were younger. I wish I could live up to the time when your people would turn you out. Muhammad asked: Will they drive me out? Waraqah answered: Anyone who came with something similar to what you have brought was treated with hostility; and if I should be alive till that day, then I would support you strongly.
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: The Pause
layers.subtitle: When revelation stopped
layers.content:
A few days later Waraqah died and the Revelation also subsided. The Prophet was caught in a mixture of emotions: despondency coupled with astonishment and bewilderment.

Al-Bukhari recorded that the Divine inspiration paused for a while and the Prophet became so sad that he intended several times to throw himself from the tops of high mountains.

Every time he went up the top of a mountain in order to throw himself down, Jibreel would appear before him and say: O Muhammad! You are indeed Allah's Messenger in truth, whereupon his heart would become tranquil and he would calm down and return home.

Ibn Hajar said: That pause was to relieve the Messenger of the fear he experienced and to make him long for the Revelation. When the bewilderment diminished, the flags of truth were raised, and Allah's Messenger knew for certain that he had become the Messenger of the Great Lord.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 93:3 — Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor is He displeased
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih Al-Bukhari 2/340 — account of the pause in revelation
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: What the first revelation means
layers.content:
The first word revealed to humanity's final Prophet was: Iqra — Read. Not pray. Not fast. Not fight. Read.

Allah chose to begin His final message with a command to engage the intellect. In a society where the Prophet himself could not read or write, the first command was about knowledge.

Khadijah's response to her frightened husband shows us what the ideal response to someone in crisis looks like: she listed his good qualities back to him. She did not question the experience. She did not dismiss it. She reminded him of who he was.

The pause in revelation, which led the Prophet to moments of profound despair, shows us that even the greatest human beings experience periods where Allah seems silent. The response of Jibreel — You are indeed Allah's Messenger in truth — was what the Prophet needed to hear. The pause was not abandonment. It was preparation for the next descent.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 96:1 — Read in the name of your Lord
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar, Darussalam

quiz.prompt: What was the exact date of the first revelation?

options.text: Ramadan 17, 609 CE
Ramadan 21, 610 CE — Monday night
Rabi al-Awwal 12, 610 CE
Rajab 27, 610 CE

quiz.citation: Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar — citing Sahih Muslim 1/368
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet was asked about fasting on Monday and replied: On it I was born, and on it the Revelation descended upon me. Birth and prophethood — both on Monday.

quiz.prompt: How many times did Jibreel squeeze the Prophet before giving him the first verses?

options.text: Once
Twice
Three times
Seven times

quiz.scholar_reflection: Three times the prophet said I cannot. Three times the angel came. The truth was not that he could not — it was that he had not yet been given what to recite. The angel gave him the words with the command.

quiz.prompt: What did Khadijah say to reassure the frightened Prophet?

options.text: You are the Prophet of Allah, do not fear
Allah will never disgrace you — you unite relations, bear burdens, help the poor, entertain guests and endure hardships in truth
What you saw was a true vision from Allah
I believe in you and will stand by you always

quiz.scholar_reflection: She argued from his character to what Allah would do. She did not say I believe you saw an angel. She said Allah will never disgrace you — and then proved it from who he was.

quiz.prompt: What did Waraqah bin Nawfal say when he heard about the revelation?

options.text: This is the devil testing you
This is the Namus — the angel who was sent to Moses
You must have imagined this in your seclusion
Go back to the cave and wait for more

quiz.citation: Sahih Al-Bukhari 1/2,3 — Waraqah bin Nawfal's response
quiz.scholar_reflection: A Christian scholar recognised Muhammad's prophethood before most of his own people. He had spent his life studying scripture and knew what to look for. Knowledge of revelation made him recognise its return.

quiz.prompt: What happened to the Prophet during the pause in revelation?

options.text: He returned to the cave of Hira and waited
He became so sad that he considered throwing himself from mountain tops
He began preaching secretly to his family
He increased his worship and fasting

quiz.scholar_reflection: The greatest human being experienced crisis, loneliness, and the terror of divine silence. This is recorded in Sahih Al-Bukhari without apology. It makes him someone we can follow.

quiz.prompt: The first revealed word was Read — to a man who could not read. What does this tell you about Allah's commands?
quiz.slider_label: How do you respond when commanded to do something you feel incapable of?

options.text: Allah's commands come with the capacity to fulfil them
The command revealed what was possible, not what already existed
Inability is not the same as impossibility when Allah commands
The Quran itself was the answer to I cannot recite

quiz.citation: Quran 96:1 — Read in the name of your Lord
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said I cannot recite three times. Then Jibreel gave him the words. The inability was true — and it did not matter. When Allah commands, the means come with the command.

quiz.prompt: Khadijah responded to the Prophet's crisis by listing his good qualities. What can you learn from this?
quiz.slider_label: How do you respond when someone close to you experiences spiritual crisis?

options.text: Remind them of their character — who they are determines what Allah will do
Do not question or challenge the experience — receive it with them
Take practical action — she took him to Waraqah for answers
All of these — Khadijah did all three

quiz.scholar_reflection: Khadijah is the model of how to support a believer in crisis. She did not panic, did not question, did not minimise. She grounded him in his own character and then sought knowledge.

quiz.prompt: The Prophet spent three years in seclusion before prophethood. What is the role of solitude in preparation?
quiz.slider_label: How much solitude do you have in your life for genuine reflection?

options.text: Solitude creates space — removing noise allows what was always there to be heard
Three years of preparation produced 23 years of prophethood
What the Prophet sought in the cave is what every human heart seeks
Taddabur — deep reflection — requires stillness that busy life does not allow

quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet's seclusion was not escape from the world. It was preparation to transform it. Three years of stillness before 23 years of movement. The silence came first.

quiz.prompt: Jibreel appeared each time the Prophet was at his lowest and said: You are indeed Allah's Messenger in truth. What does this reveal about how Allah responds to genuine despair?
quiz.slider_label: Have you ever felt Allah respond at a moment of genuine despair?

options.text: Allah intervenes at the exact moment of greatest need, not before
The words given were exactly what was needed — affirmation, not explanation
Allah did not remove the pain — He appeared within it
The pause showed how much the Quran was needed

quiz.scholar_reflection: Jibreel did not explain why revelation paused. He simply said: you are the Messenger of Allah. Sometimes what is needed is not an explanation — it is a witness. Allah sent a witness.

quiz.prompt: The first revelation commanded knowledge. Then the Prophet immediately sought human understanding through Khadijah and Waraqah. What does this tell you?
quiz.slider_label: How do you seek understanding when you experience something spiritually significant?

options.text: Revelation gives the truth — human wisdom helps contextualise it
Even the Prophet sought a scholar — there is no shame in needing guidance
Khadijah's wisdom and Waraqah's scholarship were both needed
The Prophet modelled the proper response: receive, seek understanding, act

quiz.scholar_reflection: The greatest of creation, after receiving revelation, went immediately to his wife and then to a scholar. He did not declare himself alone. He sought human wisdom alongside divine. This is the model.
